messages:
tina-support: Customer reports 502s and TLS handshake failures after yesterday's CA rotation. They see "certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain" when connecting to their private VPC endpoint. Customer supplied an openssl dump and haproxy logs.

sam-infra: Can you paste the openssl output and the exact host they're hitting? Also what rotator job id was used?

tina-support: Paste from customer: 

```
openssl s_client -showcerts -servername example-vpc.customer.internal -connect 10.1.2.3:443
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Example Root CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=example-vpc.customer.internal
   i:/C=US/O=Inter CA Ltd/CN=Example Intermediate
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...leaf...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
 1 s:/C=US/O=Inter CA Ltd/CN=Example Intermediate
   i:/C=US/O=Example Root CA/CN=Example Root CA
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...intermediate...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

tina-support: They reported it started after our rotation at ~2026-11-22 03:00 UTC (rotator job id r-20261122-03). Some hosts succeed, others fail intermittently. haproxy logs show: "SSL handshake failed (unknown CA)".

sam-infra: I'm pulling that rotator job bundle now. @opsbot can you fetch r-20261122-03 artifacts?

opsbot: rotator bundle r-20261122-03 retrieved: /artifacts/rotator/r-20261122-03/bundle.tar.gz

sam-infra: Inspecting bundle: the cert chain file for this tenant appears to include the leaf and root only; the intermediate is missing for a subset of the generated bundles. Suspect a concatenation edge-case in the bundle creator when intermediate was an empty string for some configs.

ajay-runtime: That matches symptomology: clients/proxies that depend on the server presenting the full chain will fail when intermediate is missing; other clients that fetch missing issuers from AIA/OCSP or have the intermediate cached will succeed. Explains flakiness across pools.

jen-sre: Short-term mitigation: re-upload a full chain (leaf + intermediate + root) to object storage and trigger a rotator reapply for affected edge pools. Also ask the customer to temporarily allow OCSP/CRL egress so clients can fetch issuers if needed.

sam-infra: Commands I'm running now:

```
# verify the full chain locally before upload
openssl verify -CAfile full-chain.pem leaf.pem
# re-upload to S3 (internal path)
aws s3 cp full-chain.pem s3://rotator-artifacts/r-20261122-03/tenant-abc/full-chain.pem
# trigger reapply via internal API
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/internals/rotator/reapply?r=r-20261122-03
```

sam-infra: Also noticed a DNS cache/edge IP quirk: some customer endpoints resolve to a stale proxy IP that still had a trimmed (broken) chain cached. Flushing proxy cert caches for those IPs now.

ajay-runtime: Double-check customer firewall/egress allowlists — we saw OCSP lookups timing out for a portion of traffic. If their egress blocks ocsp.exampleca.com or our S3 bucket host, they won't be able to complete validation. Advise enabling outbound to ocsp.exampleca.com and to s3-region.redwood-internal.

tina-support: I'll relay mitigation steps to customer and give an ETA. Proposed message: 1) we re-applied a fixed cert bundle server-side, 2) please allow ocsp.exampleca.com outbound for a short window, 3) run the attached openssl and curl checks and paste output if still failing.

jen-sre: Rotator reapply finished: reapply succeeded across 6 affected pools. Proxy cache flush completed. Monitoring: TLS error rate dropped to baseline over the last 10 minutes.

tina-support: Customer confirmed successful connections after we re-applied the bundle and after they temporarily allowed OCSP egress. They reported immediate recovery. Closing after 1hr stable. :thumbsup:
